# Keep vessel conversion policy overridable through Neo

## Context

The [dashboard extensibility audit](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5560546655) found that `window/VesselConversion.mjs` exports a closure factory without a Neo namespace identity. Explicit factory thresholds work, but `Neo.overwrites` does not reach it. At `dev@3a0773c9`, the only production consumer is `interaction/TabSortZone.mjs`.

## The Problem

Applications can change the exposed thresholds and composition callback, but cannot specialize the sensor's geometry or transition decisions through ordinary Neo methods without replacing/wrapping its closure. This is an unfinished extensibility outcome of #18304. The existing conversion grammar and strict asynchronous admission are valuable and must be retained.

## The Architectural Reality

`Neo.setupClass` and `Base.applyOverwrites` provide registered identity, method/default overrides and lifecycle. `IdGenerator` shows that lightweight exceptions still register through `gatekeep`; transient state does not imply exemption from namespace ownership. The [peer assessment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5560658524) requires specializing a decision without copying its lifecycle.

## The Fix

Replace the factory in its existing file with a registered `Neo.core.Base` sensor class. Keep thresholds and required admission callbacks configurable, move policy helpers to overridable methods, and retain per-instance conversion/transition state. TabSortZone creates and destroys its sensor through the existing class lifecycle. Remove the retired factory export and migrate its existing unit suite.

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| conversion policy | Base method/overwrite contract | one registered class; internal dispatch reaches overrides | default grammar unchanged | class/config/method JSDoc | overwrite and subclass controls |
| transition state | current sensor generation fence | reset and destroy invalidate late admission | explicit false retains current state | reset/destroy contract | held-promise controls |
| source ownership | TabSortZone sensor lifetime | creator destroys its sensor | no leaked registration | consumer method docs | owner teardown control |

## Decision Record impact

Aligned with ADR 0029: conversion remains transient policy over the existing outcome machine. No new outcome state, wire schema or persistence behavior.

## Decision Record

No new ADR. This implements the existing decomposition/extension outcome.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

D#18150's ownership questions 2–3: a stateful extracted owner has a bounded lifecycle and a replaceable decision surface. D#17818's selected namespace mirrors the module path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The sensor is registered at `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.VesselConversion`; Neo method/default overwrites and subclass specialization affect the executed sensor policy.
- [ ] Existing threshold, geometry, pointer-exit, hysteresis and strict synchronous/asynchronous admission controls pass unchanged in meaning.
- [ ] Reset and destroy invalidate pending transitions; late completion cannot restore conversion or mutate a destroyed sensor.
- [ ] TabSortZone owns construction and teardown; the retired factory has no production or test callers, and invalid construction does not leak a registered instance.
- [ ] The focused source/sensor suites and appropriate repository checks pass; JSDoc describes the extension points.

## Out of Scope

PreviewContract (Emmy's independent lane), Workspace decomposition, native popup adoption, dropped indicators, new lint rules, and conversion metric/threshold tuning. This is one bounded PR; no changes to merged #18383.

## Avoided Traps

Registering a wrapper around closed lexical helpers would retain the defect. Converting all eight census candidates would mix unrelated concerns. Preserving the factory alias would retain a competing extension surface.
